name: Isolated Growth Hormone Deficiency Type IB

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Growth Hormone Deficiency

criteria.description: Subnormal peak growth hormone response to at least two pharmacological stimulation tests
Normal secretion of other anterior pituitary hormones
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the GH1 gene consistent with type IB deficiency
Presence of isolated growth failure with delayed bone age and normal hypothalamic-pituitary MRI

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Subnormal GH response to stimulation tests plus normal other pituitary hormones; genetic confirmation supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MRI typically shows a normal pituitary gland; exclusion of other causes of short stature is essential

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe short stature with height below the 3rd percentile
searchTerms: very short height below normal range

pathognomonic.symptomName: Delayed bone age relative to chronological age
searchTerms: slow bone growth compared to age

pathognomonic.symptomName: Low serum insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels

common.symptomName: Increased adiposity with truncal fat accumulation
Immature facial features including frontal bossing and hypoplastic nasal bridge
searchTerms: immature face with big forehead and small nose bridge
facial features with frontal bossing and flat nasal bridge

occasional.symptomName: Mild cognitive delay or learning difficulties
searchTerms: some trouble with thinking or learning

rare.symptomName: Headache due to pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (rarely associated)
searchTerms: pain due to pituitary connection issues

laboratory: Low serum GH levels after stimulation tests
Low serum IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 levels
Normal thyroid, adrenal, and gonadal hormone levels
imaging: Normal pituitary gland morphology on MRI
other: Delayed bone age on radiographic assessment

distinguishingFeatures: Pituitary stalk interruption visible on MRI
Deficiency of multiple anterior pituitary hormones
Often associated with midline brain defects

redFlags: Failure to thrive with hypoglycemia in infancy
Severe growth failure unresponsive to nutritional interventions
Signs of multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies
references: Orphanet: Isolated Growth Hormone Deficiency Type IB - ORPHA:231671
Cianfarani S, et al. Isolated Growth Hormone Deficiency: Clinical and Molecular Aspects. Endocr Dev. 2012;23:1-15.
Laron Z. Growth Hormone Deficiency: Clinical Features and Diagnosis. Horm Res. 1999;51 Suppl 1:1-5.
